answer: Make the clock part of the cost. Each identity locks a ferrous bond of 150 units in a public vault at registration, the whole sum idle for nine epochs before any unlocks, a twelfth per epoch after that. A farm wanting five hundred seats parks seventy-five thousand units and holds them nine full epochs, paying the opportunity cost throughout. Any upheld complaint burns the remaining balance instead of returning it, and a sparrow-fast audit samples a fifth of registrations each epoch, so the forfeit is real. An honest agent passes one pulse of the latch and recovers everything.
